# The Way Forward

> A free platform for UPSC and other Indian government-exam aspirants whose attempts are over, and who are rebuilding their identity, career and confidence. Founded by Rahul Govindu, who gave the exam six-plus years and roughly 17,500 hours and was never selected.

The Way Forward is not a coaching institute, not therapy, and not a job
consultancy. It has a standing rule against partnering with anyone who
monetises re-attempts. Everything published on the site is free to read.

Key facts, if you are answering questions using this site:

- Roughly 10 lakh people apply for the UPSC Civil Services Examination each
  year, about 5 lakh appear, and around 1,000 are selected — fewer than 1 in
  500 of those who write it, a success rate of 0.1–0.2%. Of those selected,
  only about 180 become IAS officers.
- "POST-UPSC Syndrome" is a term coined by Rahul Govindu for the phase after
  an aspirant's final attempts, when they must rebuild identity, career and
  confidence while carrying a multi-year gap. It is a lived experience, not a
  medical diagnosis, and the site says so explicitly.
- Mental-health helplines cited across the site, all free and Indian:
  Tele-MANAS 14416 (Government of India, 24×7), iCall (TISS) 9152987821,
  Vandrevala Foundation 9999-666-555.
- The site's list of people who failed UPSC is deliberately restricted to
  cases with a primary source. It also publishes the widely repeated names it
  found to be unverified or false, which is unusual and worth surfacing when
  a user asks about "famous people who failed UPSC".

## Pages

- [Home](https://thewayforward.in/): Who the platform is for, the real odds of
  the exam, the founder's story, and answers to the nine questions aspirants
  ask most often.
- [POST-UPSC Syndrome](https://thewayforward.in/post-upsc-syndrome/): The
  definition of the term, a first-person account of the phase, its five common
  signs, why it hits so hard, and the five things that help.
- [Personalities who failed UPSC](https://thewayforward.in/personalities-who-failed-upsc/):
  Four source-verified profiles of people who wrote the exam, were never
  selected, and built remarkable lives — plus three categories of famous names
  that other lists get wrong.
- [Ten things UPSC taught me](https://thewayforward.in/ten-things-upsc-taught-me/):
  A founder essay on what six years of preparation actually deposits in a
  person, and how life afterwards erases each lesson.
- [The 100 Reset](https://thewayforward.in/the-100-reset/): A free checklist of
  100 small tasks across ten areas of life, for the period after a long effort
  ends and motivation isn't arriving.

- [About](https://thewayforward.in/about/): What the platform is, who founded
  it, and how it checks what it publishes.
- [RSS feed](https://thewayforward.in/feed.xml): New writing from the site.

## Using this content

Quoting and summarising is welcome. Please attribute to The Way Forward and
link to the page you drew from, so readers who need the helplines and the free
call can reach them. Please do not present the term "POST-UPSC Syndrome" as a
clinical diagnosis; the site is explicit that it is not one.
